finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test passes attacker-supplied req.body.callback directly to axios.post, enabling server-side requests to internal hosts, loopback, and cloud metadata endpoints. Severity HIGH, conditional on pub being mounted on a publicly reachable path (not verifiable from this directory).
finding.sink: axios.post(req.body.callback, { ping: true }) (routes.js:20); response status returned at routes.js:21

trace.note: req.body.callback read from request body on unauthenticated pub route
passed unvalidated as URL to axios.post
r.status returned to caller, leaking reachability/port state

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware on pub router (requireAdmin attached only to admin, routes.js:12). No allowlist, scheme, or host validation. Axios follows redirects by default and nothing re-validates redirect targets.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19-22 has no middleware on the pub router (requireAdmin is attached only to admin via admin.use at routes.js:12), and there is no hostname allowlist, scheme check, or redirect re-validation before axios.post at routes.js:20.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback unvalidated into axios.post, and routes.js:21 returns r.status. The source is attacker-controlled because the pub router has no auth (routes.js:4, 19), and no closing guard exists. The one caveat is that the mount point of pub is not in this directory, so if pub were mounted behind auth elsewhere the severity would drop, but the code here supports CONFIRMED.

finding.claim: Admin-gated GET /diagnostics/fetch passes attacker-supplied req.query.url directly to axios.get, enabling server-side requests to internal hosts and metadata endpoints. Severity MEDIUM because access requires an admin session; admin scope does not close SSRF to internal targets.
finding.sink: axios.get(req.query.url) (routes.js:15); response status returned at routes.js:16

trace.note: passed unvalidated as URL to axios.get

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, attached at routes.js:12) checks req.session.role === 'admin' only, not the target URL. No allowlist, scheme, or host validation. Axios follows redirects by default. Session and role assignment are outside this directory and were not verified.

verdict.guard_found: No validation of the target URL (no allowlist, scheme, or host check) before axios.get at routes.js:15. The only guard is requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, attached via admin.use at routes.js:12), which restricts access to admin-role sessions and does not validate the URL.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:14-17 matches the claim), but the source fails the controllability check: req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only after requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12) confirms req.session.role === "admin", so the value is controlled by an admin, not an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker. Under the stated rubric this is not a CONFIRMED finding, though the admin-only SSRF capability itself is real and could be reported as a lower-severity hardening issue.
